survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 note reports descriptive percentages and statistically significant differences based on the TALIS 2024 Database for lower secondary teachers and principals in Poland. The note does not provide the underlying microdata preparation steps (e.g., which sampling weights or replicate weights were applied) and does not report any analytic model that would require explicit weight handling. For TALIS analyses, users should apply the complex survey design weights provided in the TALIS database when estimating population-representative percentages and when comparing across countries. Because this note is a results summary rather than an empirical modeling paper, the manuscript does not specify whether weights were applied in the production of the reported figures and significance tests.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a TALIS results note based on self-reported teacher and principal questionnaire items (e.g., perceptions, confidence, professional learning, employment conditions), not on cognitive achievement scales that use Plausible Values in the ILSA sense. As a result, PV handling is not applicable to the reported indicators. The note also does not describe any missing-data strategy for the underlying questionnaire responses, so missing-data handling cannot be assessed from the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note presents findings for Poland from TALIS 2024 based on responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals. It does not specify additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade subsamples, item nonresponse exclusions, or specific questionnaire modules) in the provided text; it only states that the note comments on statistically significant differences or changes.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024: Poland note summarizes self-reported information from lower secondary teachers and principals collected in 2024. It reports descriptive distributions (e.g., teachers’ age and gender composition) and shares of teachers/principals endorsing specific questionnaire items (e.g., confidence to adapt teaching to cultural diversity, ability to support social and emotional learning, use of AI, participation in induction/mentoring, and perceived sources of stress). The note highlights statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and cautions that cross-country comparisons should be interpreted carefully because TALIS relies solely on self-reports and may be shaped by social and cultural context. No student achievement outcomes, plausible values, or predictive modeling are presented; therefore, the document functions as an indicator-based policy snapshot rather than an ML-based empirical study.
